messages.subject: Use RCytoscape to display 'legend' (i.e., informational) nodes
messages.subject_clean: Use RCytoscape to display 'legend' (i.e., informational) nodes
messages.body_plain:
I have just added a cookbook recipe (some simple code accompanied by
explanations) for adding a 'legend node' to your display.

To quote from the recipe:

In traditional use of Cytoscape, every node is a 'data' node: it
represents a molecule or a process, or some other analytical entity.
Just as in map-making, we sometimes want more. You may wish to put up
a legend, or some explanatory text, perhaps a prominent label saying,
i.e.,

"Time point 3 (8 hours)"
"Low Oxygen"
"Patient 5"
Here is how to do that. As usual, I demonstrate this in the context of
the makeSimpleGraph () (see 'methods' for more information about this
built-in RCytoscape utility function).
g = RCytoscape::makeSimpleGraph ()
g = graph::addNode ('info.node', g)
nodeData (g, 'info.node', 'label') = 'information will be written
here'
window.title = 'Legend Demo'
cw = new.CytoscapeWindow (window.title, graph=g)
displayGraph (cw)
layout (cw, "jgraph-spring")
redraw (cw)

# now set up the appearance of the informational node, using a bunch
of 'direct' calls
setNodeShapeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 'rect')
setNodeSizeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 140)
setNodeFontSizeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 32);
setNodeLabelDirect (cw, 'info.node', '')
setNodeColorDirect (cw, 'info.node', '#FFEEFF')
fitContent (cw)
redraw (cw)

# now change and update the message in the information node a few
times
for (i in 1:10) {
  random.int <http://random.int> = as.integer (100 * runif (1))
  new.label = paste ('random label', random.int <http://random.int>)
  setNodeLabelDirect (cw, 'info.node', new.label)
  redraw (cw)
  system ('sleep 1')
  }

messages.subject: save.layout, restore.layout functions
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This will be included in the next version of the package, but if you
need this sooners, here are a couple of very compact functions for
saving & restoring layouts:

save.layout = function (cw, filename) {
   custom.layout = getPosition (cw,  getAllNodes (cw))
   save (custom.layout, file=filename)
   }

restore.layout = function (cw, filename) {
   load (filename)
   node.names = names (custom.layout)
   x = as.integer (sapply (custom.layout, function (node.loc) return
(node.loc$x)))
   y = as.integer (sapply (custom.layout, function (node.loc) return
(node.loc$y)))
   setPosition (cw, node.names, x, y)
   }

messages.subject: hide/unhide vs delete [was Re: tell when you have enough for the day :-)]
messages.subject_clean: hide/unhide vs delete [was Re: tell when you have enough for the day :-)]
messages.body_plain:
Hi Burak,

After RCy tells Cytoscape to 'hide' nodes, you can get them back -- though they lose their position.

With 'deleteSelectedNodes' they are gone forever.

Here is how it works for hide/unhide:

 cw <- new.CytoscapeWindow ('unhideAll.test', graph=makeSimpleGraph())
  displayGraph (cw)
  layout (cw, 'jgraph-spring')
  redraw (cw)
  clearSelection (cw)
  selectNodes (cw, 'A')
  hideSelectedNodes (cw)
  system ('sleep 2')   # see that 'A' is no longer visible
  unhideAll (cw)       # notice the odd location Cytoscape uses for A

Given that the layout is lost with hide/unhide, you might want to bracket your code with

   save.layout (cw, 'layout.before.hiding')
   .... # your code here
   restore.layout (cw, 'layout.before.hiding')

 - Paul

large display area. This will also be the area that is shown in the
export. Combined with a large zoom level this should give you want you
want. You could later re-sample the picture at a higher resolution to
make the image 'smaller'.

Jan

I would like to add node attribute data to an existing graph.  The code below attempts to add "Copy.Number"  - a set of numerical attributes -  to an existing graph, but it does not work.  Is there a way to do this?

getWindowList(cy)

g2 <- getGraph (w2)
g2 = initNodeAttribute (g2, 'Copy.Number', 'numeric', 1.0)
nodeData (g2, n=as.character(tt$Gene.Name), attr='Copy.Number') <- as.numeric(tt$Copy.Number)
addGraphToGraph(w2, g2)
displayGraph(w2)

Thanks for your help,

Mark Grimes

messages.subject: Re: RCyKEGG
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert,

RCyKEGG is actually a package in its own right, but one that I have yet not submitted to CRAN or bioc.  It has a vignette, unitTests and a reasonable set of man pages.

It's attached below.  It builds upon Jitao David Zhang's very useful KEGGgraph package.

To get started:

   R CMD install RCyKEGG_1.0.7.tar.gz
   start R
   library (RCyKEGG)
     # run the unitTests, just to be sure that everything is working
   RCyKEGG:::.test ()
     # or go straight to using it yourself, by looking at the vignette and help pages
   browseVignettes ('RCyKEGG')
   help (package='RCyKEGG')

Questions, suggestions and bug reports always welcome.

 - Paul

messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
messages.body_plain:
Hi Burak,

I've had similar experiences.  It seems that Cytoscape 2.x locks in certain vizmap settings, in not always predictable ways.

For instance, if you set a visual attribute using one of the direct calls (i.e., setNodeColorDirect) then there is no way to undo it later, and go back to mapping rules.

My solution is awkward:  I develop Cytoscape maps (networks, that is, with vizmapping and layout) driven all from R.  When I get in a jam, as you have being unable to reset the default node color, I shut down Cytoscape, restart, and regenerate things.

It may be that a judicious use of visual styles will accomplish this end too.  I'll experiment and let you know.

It's also possible that the good (& busy!) people developing Cytoscape 3 will be interested in this use case.

Cheers!

 - Paul

I think you can work around this by deleting the visual attribute of the
node for which you set a particular property. The visual mapping system
should notice this and should redraw the graph using the standard
settings of the visual mapper that you're using (you might need to redraw).

Have you tried that?

Cheers,

Jan

On 06/28/2011 11:46 PM, Paul Shannon wrote:
> Hi Burak,
>
> I've had similar experiences.  It seems that Cytoscape 2.x locks in certain vizmap settings, in not always predictable ways.
>
> For instance, if you set a visual attribute using one of the direct calls (i.e., setNodeColorDirect) then there is no way to undo it later, and go back to mapping rules.
>
> My solution is awkward:  I develop Cytoscape maps (networks, that is, with vizmapping and layout) driven all from R.  When I get in a jam, as you have being unable to reset the default node color, I shut down Cytoscape, restart, and regenerate things.
>
> It may be that a judicious use of visual styles will accomplish this end too.  I'll experiment and let you know.
>
> It's also possible that the good (&  busy!) people developing Cytoscape 3 will be interested in this use case.
>
> Cheers!
>
>   - Paul
>
> On Jun 28, 2011, at 2:07 PM, Burak Kutlu wrote:
>
>> HI
>> I am trying to reset all the color rules by:
>>
>> setDefaultNodeColor(cw, '#FFFFFF', vizmap.style.name <http://vizmap.style.name> = "default")
>> [1] TRUE
>>> redraw(cw)
>> But this does not seem to change anything, Is this the expected behavior=?
>>
>> Thanks!
>> -burak

messages.subject: Re: reset the node color rule
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul,

there is the delete[Node|Edge|Network]Attribute function but this
deletes the attribute for all nodes. What happens when you just delete
the content of the attribute in the attribute browser (in the GUI)?

Cheers,

Jan
